messages.content: Write the first page of an onboarding document for a new backend engineer joining a payments team. Around 200 words.

# Welcome to Payments

Your first week is about pushing one test payment all the way through the system yourself, from the API call to the settlement row.

We own four services. `charge-api` takes the request and validates it. `ledger` records double-entry postings and is the source of truth for every balance. `psp-gateway` talks to Stripe and Adyen. `recon` reads settlement files each morning and yells when they disagree with the ledger.

Two rules matter more than anything else you will read here. Money moves only through the ledger, never by mutating a balance column. And every write to `psp-gateway` carries an idempotency key derived from the charge ID, because the network will retry and the card network will not forgive you twice.

Get your local stack running first (`make dev`, then `make seed`). The runbook in `docs/local-setup.md` is current as of last month; if a step fails, fix the doc in the same PR.

Your onboarding ticket is PAY-4412, adding a currency field to the refund endpoint. It touches three of the four services, which is the point.

Ask Priya about the ledger, Tom about anything PSP-shaped, and me about everything else. Standup is 9:45.
Add a section on who to ask for what.

output:
Here's the section. It replaces the closing "Ask Priya about the ledger" line, which was doing this job badly.

# Who to ask

Priya owns the ledger. Postings, balance queries, why one charge produced four rows instead of two, and any schema change under `ledger/` — all Priya. Do not merge a migration there without a review from Priya, even a trivial one.

Tom covers everything PSP-shaped: Stripe and Adyen quirks, webhook replay, sandbox credentials, and the reason a card decline arrives twice with different codes.

Dani runs recon and the settlement pipeline. If a morning alert fires and you cannot tell whether the file or the ledger is wrong, that is a Dani question, not a debugging exercise for you.

For deploys, staging access, and anything in Terraform, ask in `#pay-infra` rather than picking a person. Someone there is on rotation.

Money is moving wrong in production: page the on-call in `#pay-incident` first, then tell me. Do not investigate quietly for twenty minutes hoping it resolves.

Everything else, or anything you cannot place, comes to me. Asking in week one costs nothing.
